messages:
AcmeCorp SRE: Hey team — starting 09:10 UTC our prod app started failing calls to Redwood Private API. Failures are 502/403 from downstream services that only allow our egress IPs. We haven't changed anything. Can you confirm if Redwood egress IPs changed for our VPC?

Elaine (Support): Hi @AcmeCorp SRE :wave: — sorry about the outage. Please paste a curl showing the failure and one of the IPs you have on your allowlist. Also which region is your deployment?

AcmeCorp SRE: We're in us-west-2. Our allowlist contains: 52.24.18.91 and 52.24.18.92. Here's a quick repro from our app host:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://private-api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -o /dev/null -s -w "%{http_code}\n"
# -> 502
# tcpdump shows outbound src IP 3.120.45.77
```

Elaine (Support): Thanks — that outbound IP (3.120.45.77) is not in the allowlist you shared. Can you run a quick external IP check from the host and paste output? e.g. `dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com` or `curl https://ifconfig.co`

AcmeCorp SRE: Ran both: `3.120.45.77`. We see that in our logs now. We suspect a NAT swap.

Vivek (SRE): @Elaine / @Chris — I can see a NAT migration event in the infra logs around 09:08 UTC for that tenant's private deployment in us-west-2. Looks like the cloud provider replaced the underlying NAT instance and the ephemeral EIP changed before the customer pinned an EIP. This caused outbound IP drift. I'll post the infra audit snippet.

deploy-bot: [infra-audit] tenant=acmecorp id=tn-8821 event=nat-replace timestamp=1769876400 old_eip=52.24.18.92 new_eip=3.120.45.77 reason=provider-maintenance

Chris (NetOps): Confirming — provider maintenance forced a NAT host replacement. For private deployments we recommend customers pin an Elastic IP on their NAT gateway to prevent this. Looks like AcmeCorp used our default NAT without EIP pinning.

Elaine (Support): Action plan: 1) I'll ask AcmeCorp to temporarily add 3.120.45.77 to their allowlist so calls succeed immediately. 2) We'll open an internal task to pin a stable egress IP for this tenant or advise them to attach a customer-owned EIP. 3) Create an incident and update the support portal egress list for their org. @Vivek can you pin in the egress pool or provide the stable range?

Vivek (SRE): Pinned a static EIP to the tenant's NAT at 09:35 UTC and added the stable egress IP range to the tenant metadata: stable-egress=3.120.45.77. I also created INC-4521 and assigned to eng-infra. Temporary measure: keep both old and new IPs in allowlist for 72 hours.

AcmeCorp SRE: Added 3.120.45.77 and traffic immediately recovered. Thanks. Can you confirm whether this was a Redwood-initiated change or provider-driven so we can update our runbook?

Vivek (SRE): Provider-driven maintenance; the NAT replacement was not a deliberate Redwood-initiated change. We should update the onboarding docs to recommend EIP pinning for Private deployments and add a note about checking `dig +short myip.opendns.com` after maintenance.

Elaine (Support): Follow-ups: - INC-4521 created and linked to the customer case. - Support portal updated with the temporary egress IP list. - Docs ticket DOCS-198 to add EIP pinning recommendation. Marking this thread for postmortem if customer requests. :thumbsup:

AcmeCorp SRE: All good for now — please keep us posted on any further egress changes. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Chris (NetOps): Noted. Will implement a monitoring alert to notify tenants if outbound IPs change unexpectedly.

deploy-bot: incident INC-4521 status=acknowledged assignee=eng-infra priority=high

Elaine (Support): Closing the support ticket once docs and incident follow-ups are in motion. If anything else crops up, ping this thread.
